The Park That Refuses to Reach Pallavi

# The Park That Refuses to Reach Pallavi

### How Mylapore's Nageswara Rao Park entered an endless Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi, leaving Mylapore's walkers permanently in the Anupallavi.

[](https://substack.com/@amaruvi)

![Amaruvi Devanathan's avatar](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Bq_i!,w_36,h_36,c_fill,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F357700fd-8e69-44fa-a5f8-000e6e26808a_1002x1002.jpeg)

Every morning my wife asks me : “Walk or Park Inspection?” - The sad reality of Nageswara Rao Park renovation.

These days, there isn’t much difference.

I’m fifty-four.

Professionally, I’m a software architect.

Emotionally, I’m a writer.

Spiritually, I’m a heritage conservation enthusiast.

Physically, I’m an exercise enthusiast. I practise passive resistance to exercise. I’m not lazy; my body is simply in data-saver mode.

Every January I buy imported walking shoes that cost more than my first scooter -( the one ‘Activa’ that became ‘Passiva’ due to Mylapore’s craters.)

Every February the shoes become premium indoor footwear.

By March, they achieve spiritual enlightenment inside the shoe rack. Life Cycle completed.

Yet every morning, armed with optimism, a Fitbit, and two cups of filter coffee, I march towards Nageswara Rao Park like a freedom fighter.

Only to be greeted by barricades.

I think the barricades know me by name now.

The security guard smiled at me the other day.

“Sir... still closed. Same status”

I smiled back.

“So is my waistline.”

Both of us accepted reality without another word.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

People from outside Mylapore imagine this is just another neighbourhood park.

Poor souls.

Nageswara Rao Park is not a park.

It is Parliament.

It is the Music Academy minus T.M.Krishna politics.

It is a health club where nobody loses weight.

It is a retirement planning conference.

It is LinkedIn for retired bankers..

It is Facebook without the internet.

It is where cholesterol reports are discussed with the seriousness of the Union Budget.

Where else can you overhear one gentleman explaining LDL levels while another interrupts him to argue that Semmangudi’s Kamboji in 1965 was superior to the 1967 version?

Nobody finds this unusual.

This is simply how Mylapore functions.

Walking is merely the background process.

Conversation is the main application.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every regular has a role.

Retired SBI Srinivasan is our unofficial historian.

He compares every modern event with something that happened in 1987. Everything reminds him of 1987 — including the price of filter coffee.

He has a PhD in comparing current events to 1987. If the world ends, he’ll say it happened better in ’87. His memory is sharp. Only that his sense of time is stuck in the last century.

I ask him about the park repair matter - renovation as they say.

“This renovation? They repainted the benches in one Sunday back then.”

“In 1987 Sir?” I ask meekly.

Nobody remembers the benches.

Nobody asked.

Yet the information arrives every morning like All India Radio.

Then comes GitHub Gopalan.

Officially, he is a software architect.

Unofficially, he believes every civic problem can be solved with Agile methodology and a dashboard.

He refuses to call this a renovation.

“It’s a Digital Transformation Programme.”

He lowered his voice one morning.

“They skipped User Acceptance Testing.”

“The users being...?”

“We are.”

“And did anybody ask us?”

He looked offended.

“That is not how Agile works anymore.”

------------------------------------------------------------------------

As software engineers, we understand project delays.

Requirements change.

Budgets shrink.

Clients suddenly discover a “small enhancement” that requires rewriting the entire application.

But this project has gone beyond software engineering.

It has entered Carnatic music.

The renovation began like a brisk Hamsadhwani varnam.

Within weeks, it became a leisurely Kambhoji alapana.

Today it has evolved into a full Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi.

Unfortunately, only the Ragam has been completed.

The Tanam appears endless.

The Pallavi has been postponed until further notice.

Even Ariyakudi would have looked at this pace and said,

“Could we move to the next sangati before retirement?”

GitHub Gopalan insists the contractor has invented a new methodology called **Agile in Chatur Maasya Kalam**.

Each sprint lasts four months.

The daily stand-up happens without any visible team.

The burndown chart has been replaced by actual burned leaves.

GitHub Gopalan doesn’t complain about delays. He just calls it ‘extended sprint’ or at times ‘scope creep’.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The displaced walkers now roam the streets of East Abhiramapuram like refugees from an abandoned civilisation.

Imagine seventy senior citizens attempting brisk walking while simultaneously debating whether Sanjay Subrahmanyan’s Bhairavi surpassed Cleveland Gopalan’s.

Traffic is merely an accompaniment.

One gentleman narrowly avoids a scooter without interrupting his analysis of neraval singing.

Only in Mylapore can someone dodge an MTC bus without losing shruti.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Poor Yoga Jagannathan.

He invested in an imported yoga mat.

Now he performs Surya Namaskar between two parked scooters. From Surya Namaskaram, he has migrated to Scooter Namaskaram in his avatar as a parking-lot yogi. His Surya Namaskar now includes obstacle avoidance training.

Every downward movement has become an extreme sport.

Kutcheri Kalyani still reviews concerts while walking. Even the barricades can’t stop her concert analysis.

“Yesterday’s RTP was magnificent.” - RTP = Ragam, Tanam, Pallavi.

“What about this RTP?” I asked, pointing at the barricades.

She looked at the closed park.

“This one seems determined never to reach the Pallavi.”

Even the crows appeared to appreciate that joke.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The squirrels are perhaps the greatest victims.

One particularly dignified fellow (I call him Narasimhan) used to inspect every bench like a quality assurance engineer - the most dignified unemployed QA engineer in Mylapore

Now he sits outside the compound wall looking forlorn, like a 45 year old software engineer who needs to learn AI in two days.

Yesterday I looked at him sympathetically.

He flicked his tail.

Years of software development have taught me to interpret non-verbal feedback.

It clearly meant,

“Funding delay.”

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The real sadness isn’t the inconvenience.

It is the interruption of something that already worked beautifully.

For years, this little oasis had been lovingly cared for. Trees matured. Birds returned every morning. Children grew up on its pathways. Weekend kutcheris became part of Mylapore’s cultural rhythm. Civic discussions flourished beneath its shade. Quiet stewardship—including the generous support extended over the years by Sundaram Finance—helped preserve one of Chennai’s rare urban sanctuaries.

Then somebody decided that what needed careful maintenance perhaps required dramatic transformation. Like they say ‘Strategic Platform Migration’ in every Town Hall in every Software Company, from time immemorial.

Most walkers I know never asked for a grand makeover.

If a bench was broken, repair the bench.

If a pathway cracked, repair the pathway.

Nobody has ever suggested replacing filter coffee with cappuccino simply because it looks more modern.

Why should parks be treated differently?

And why demolish everything and rebuild ? Are you in software where we re-write the entire application to fix a bug ? What ha ?

And they are cutting down trees in the park and installing air-conditioned-gym. Something like .. leave it .. any reference to politics is prohibited in Amaruvi’s Mylapore Inquirer essays.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Last Sunday our entire walking group gathered outside the locked gates.

It felt like devotees arriving at a temple only to discover that the deity was under renovation.

One gentleman sighed.

“I miss the trees.”

Another said,

“I miss the kutcheris.”

A third whispered,

“I miss doing absolutely nothing on that bench.” (He was a software engineer who was eternally on bench ).

The fourth quietly admitted,

“I miss the toilets.”

Every group eventually arrives at truth.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

I still wear my walking shoes every morning.

Not because I believe the park will reopen that day.

Because hope is the default operating system of every Mylapore resident.

Like one day, the roads would be laid. One day the mosquitoes would migrate.

Like one day the traffic would not be stopped for the Chief Minister’s convoy.

Like one day the state’s registration department would not demand bribes.

Like that :

One day those gates will open.

The retired bankers will resume solving India’s economy.

Software engineers will conduct unsolicited project reviews.

Carnatic rasikas will debate recordings that nobody else remembers.

Yoga Jagannathan will continue looking fitter than he feels.

I will continue looking more athletic than I actually am.

Coffee will once again defeat cholesterol.

Life will return to its wonderfully inefficient rhythm.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Until then, I walk up to the barricades every morning.

The same old crow sits on the rain tree.

He looks at us.

He looks at the closed gate.

“What is the status?” I ask him.

After a delay ( probably latency ), he says,

“Caw”, with a look of the only honest stakeholder in this entire renovation saga.

Every Mylaporean Software Engineer interprets this as:

**“Release postponed... again.”**

So, I come home and update my WhatsApp status thus :

“**My waistline and the park share the same status: Under Renovation**.”
